newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SPANISH DUO THREATEN REPEAT OF 1994.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH DUO THREATEN REPEAT OF 1994.

text.p: Spain's Sergi Bruguera and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario rekindled memories of three years ago as the former French Open champions sailed smoothly into the third round of the grand slam event on Thursday with straight set wins.

Three years ago Bruguera and Sanchez Vicario capped off a dominating fortnight by the Spaniards who occupied three-of-four places in the semifinals then claimed both crowns in front of an audience that included the King of Spain.

Bruguera, who struggled with an ankle injury last season and plummeted out of the top 20 for the first time since 1990, continued to enjoy a renaissance on the French clay, crushing Dennis van Scheppingen of the Netherlands 6-2 6-3 6-3.
Sanchez Vicario, meanwhile, moved a step closer to her fourth consecutive appearance in the finals demolishing Japan's Ai Sugiyama 6-3 6-1.
When Bruguera, seeded 16th, arrived in Paris he was not considered the most serious Spanish threat to lift the French title with five of his countrymen ranked in front of him.
But as the tournament heads towards its second week, the two-time champion, winner of back-to-back titles in 1993 and 1994, is looking more and more capable of claiming a third.
"It's easier here when you're playing with confidence, it doesn't matter whether you are the favourite or not," said Bruguera, a finalist at Key Biscayne.
"I'm not dreaming of winning this tournament but I want to win it again." he added. "It's the tournament I want to win the most."

Sanchez Vicario, who has struggled this season and only advanced as far as the semifinals of two of the 11 tournaments she has entered, has returned to her familiar tenacious form in Paris, crushing both her opponents in two sets and dropping a total of just five games along the way.
"That's the past, I'm just concentrating on my play here," she said. "This tournament is two weeks and anything can happen in two weeks.
"The most important thing at the moment is that I'm feeling and playing good."
